findings.title: Disabled SQL expressions are logged as DuckDB serialization errors
findings.body: Classic dashboard and alerting SQL expressions do not use the new ReadQuery gate. They call NewSQLCommand, which always calls TablesList. TablesList still interpolates the raw user expression into a DuckDB statement (`SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')`, with only single quotes doubled) and passes it to RunCommands. The new stub always returns "not implemented", so the statement is not executed, but the error branch always logs both the raw expression and that command at error level. NewSQLCommand logs the raw SQL again at warn. Every panel refresh or alert evaluation of an existing SQL expression therefore emits error logs containing the full user SQL (including any literals) and looks like an outage rather than an intentional disable for CVE-2024-9264. Reject the expression before building or logging that statement.

findings.title: Security disable is reported as an unreadable SQL command
findings.body: Because TablesList now always fails, every non-empty SQL expression on the SSE path (dashboards and alerting) is returned as errutil.BadRequest "sql-invalid-sql" with public message "error reading SQL command". That message is wrong: the expression was not malformed, and the underlying stub error is discarded. Callers, alert error states, and users cannot tell a CVE-2024-9264 kill switch from a bad query, so they will debug or rewrite valid expressions instead of removing a disabled feature. Return a single explicit disabled error from NewSQLCommand and UnmarshalSQLCommand.

findings.title: SQL disablement is reported as not implemented and ignores the flag
findings.body: ReadQuery rejects every SQL expression with "sqlExpressions is not implemented". The feature existed and is being turned off for CVE-2024-9264; the text is false. enableSqlExpressions also ignores FlagSqlExpressions: it negates IsEnabledGlobally and then returns false from both branches, and it dereferences h.features before that, so a nil toggle service panics instead of returning this error. Enabling the documented sqlExpressions flag does not change the result and is not mentioned. Clients that only read the toggle still believe the feature is available, then get a message that does not explain the security disable.

findings.title: No regression test that SQL expressions stay disabled
findings.body: This is the CVE-2024-9264 fix, but no test was added or updated. NewSQLCommand is the dashboard and alerting entry point and now fails only because the stub's RunCommands returns an error; ReadQuery depends on enableSqlExpressions, which always returns false through an inverted flag check. Nothing asserts that both entry points reject SQL when sqlExpressions is on and when it is off, or that Execute does not run user SQL. A later change can restore DuckDB or make the helper honor the flag without CI failing, which would reintroduce the RCE/LFI. Add a regression test for both paths that expects an explicit disabled error and does not need the duckdb binary.
